title: First Return of the Prepared Evaluation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $w,s,o$ be Boolean words. Suppose $M$ computes output $o$ from input $s$ in exactly $T$ steps. The evaluator, prepared with candidate input $s$ and run on input $w$, first reaches its return state at some positive time $t\le 1+2T+|s|+2$; before that time it is never in the return state, and at time $t$ its configuration is the evaluator configuration of the halted tracked computation after the candidate input head has been scanned to the right boundary.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$M$ computes output $o$ from $s$ in exactly $T$ steps
replaced:
Let $M$ compute output $o$ on argument $s$ within time $T$, and consider the capture-
wrapped evaluator of the right-boundary wrapper of the tracked evaluator of $M$, started
on the prepared candidate seam for $s$. Then there is a positive time $t \le 1 + 2T +
|s| + 2$ such that the evaluator does not visit its return state before $t$ and at time
$t$ is exactly the evaluator configuration of the halted, right-normalized tracked
endpoint: full trace banks, complete capture buffer, and candidate head at the right
boundary.
